speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you've had difficulty wearing earrings and experienced shooting ear pain following a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain is triggered by touching the ear or inserting an object?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically involving the V3 branch/mandibular division) secondary to post-tympanoplasty neuropathic pain or aberrant regeneration.

I note your history of recurrent ear infections and the specific trigger of eating; were the "shooting pain" episodes sudden, electric-shock like, and did they last only a few seconds? Also, did you experience any facial numbness or weakness since your surgery?
